description: How much credit support and revenue-share-backed capacity will NVIDIA have committed to AI cloud partners under its new revenue-sharing and credit-support business model?
outcome: Total dollar amount of credit support / revenue-share-backed capacity NVIDIA has committed to AI cloud operators under the announced model, as disclosed in its filings.
period: Next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027, reported ~February 2027); set as the next annual report because the model is presented as already being introduced/underway.

description: How large is NVIDIA's equity investment in Intel, and will the $5 billion stake be completed and held at that level as disclosed in NVIDIA's filings?
outcome: The dollar amount of NVIDIA's equity stake in Intel and whether the reported $5 billion investment is completed, as disclosed in NVIDIA's next annual report and any related 8-K / Schedule 13D-G filings.
period: Next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027, reported ~February 2027); set as the next annual report because the item presents the $5 billion as an equity investment/commitment allocated to Intel, i.e. a sized stake tracked by its amount at that report.

description: Will the US government keep in force, broaden, or tighten its approval allowing Nvidia to sell some of its semiconductors to China under specified conditions, and at what scale will those permitted China sales occur?
outcome: Whether US export-control approval for Nvidia semiconductor sales to China remains in force, is expanded, or is restricted, and the resulting scale of Nvidia's permitted China sales.
period: Fiscal year ending late January 2027 (reported ~February 2027); set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision, checked against US export-control rule updates and Nvidia's China revenue disclosure.

description: Will Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin AI chip platform reach first customer shipments — the step that brings its revenue — by the end of 2026?
outcome: First customer shipments / initial revenue from Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, confirmed by the company.
period: End of 2026 (item says Vera Rubin 'could begin shipping later this year'); checked against Nvidia's quarterly reports and management confirmation of initial Vera Rubin shipments.

description: Will the combined data center capital expenditures of the 'big four' AI hyperscalers for calendar 2026 come in near the ~$650 billion the item reports they plan to spend?
outcome: The big four AI hyperscalers' aggregated calendar-2026 data center capital expenditure versus the ~$650 billion plan reported in the item, with Nvidia's own projection of ~$1 trillion for 2027 as the forward reference.
period: Full-year calendar 2026, checked against the hyperscalers' capex disclosures in their Q4 2026 earnings reports (reported roughly January–February 2027); the item gives no release date, so the check date is set by the companies' own year-end reporting.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture, the rack system slated to debut with its Vera Rubin Ultra generation, reach first customer shipments, and in which year — 2027 as originally slated or 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: First customer shipments of Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack architecture (Vera Rubin Ultra generation), confirmed by the company, versus the reported more-than-12-month delay to 2028.
period: 2028 — the date SemiAnalysis reports for Kyber's delayed debut, against the original 2027 schedule stated in the item; checked against Nvidia's quarterly reports and management confirmation of initial Kyber/Rubin Ultra shipments.

description: Will commodity DRAM (and by extension graphics memory) contract prices rise further through calendar 2026, deepening the memory shortage that is raising GPU makers' memory input costs?
outcome: Direction and magnitude of commodity DRAM/graphics memory contract prices over calendar 2026, and whether the shortage that has forced NVIDIA to revive an older graphics card persists through the year.
period: Full-year calendar 2026 — the item states the DRAM crisis 'intensifies in 2026'; checked against Q4 2026 DRAM contract price releases (TrendForce/DRAMeXchange) and memory makers' Q4 2026 results, reported roughly January 2027.

description: How large will NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments be at its next annual report, and could that obligation pressure its cash or credit position if AI demand disappoints?
outcome: Total dollar amount of NVIDIA's supply purchase commitments disclosed at its next annual report, against the ~$119 billion the item cites as the current reference.
period: Next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027, reported ~February 2027); set as the next annual report because the supply commitments are presented as already undertaken/outstanding.

description: What share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator spending will go to domestic suppliers (Huawei, Hygon, Cambricon and others) over the 12 months from mid-2026, and how far will Nvidia's share of the Chinese accelerator market fall from its present level?
outcome: The share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator budgets allocated to domestic products versus the ~30% baseline reported in the July 2026 Bloomberg Intelligence survey, and the direction of Nvidia's share of that market, as reported in follow-up surveys and Nvidia's disclosed China revenue.
period: The 12 months following the survey's release on 2026-07-07 (through roughly mid-2027); set by the survey's stated 'next 12 months' horizon, checked against follow-up Bloomberg Intelligence surveys and Nvidia's quarterly China revenue disclosures over that window.

description: Will the spot price for an hour on an Nvidia H100 GPU continue to fall through calendar 2026, extending the drop from its May 2026 peak of about $3.20?
outcome: Direction of the H100 GPU hourly spot rental price through calendar 2026, specifically whether it remains below the ~$3.20/hour May 2026 peak and continues the steady decline.
period: Year-end 2026; set as the check date for whether the H100 spot price remains below the May 2026 peak of about $3.20/hour, using Ornn/compute marketplace spot price data.

description: Will China's government allow selected Chinese AI firms (including Alibaba Group Holding) to buy Nvidia H200 GPUs, and at what scale, replacing the current restriction that bars Chinese firms from purchasing the device?
outcome: Whether Beijing implements its reported plan to permit selected Chinese companies to buy limited numbers of Nvidia H200 GPUs, the scale of permitted purchases, and any subsequent broadening or tightening versus the current restriction.
period: Fiscal year ending late January 2027 (reported ~February 2027); set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision, because the item gives no date for Beijing's authorisation.

description: Will France's competition authority (Autorité de la concurrence) conclude its antitrust investigation into Nvidia's cloud-AI and GPU practices by issuing a formal decision — a statement of objections, fine or behavioural remedies — rather than closing the case without action?
outcome: A formal decision, or closure without action, by the French competition authority in its antitrust investigation into Nvidia's alleged anti-competitive practices in cloud-AI and GPU markets, including any fine or remedy imposed.
period: Nvidia's fiscal year ending late January 2027 (FY2027, reported ~February 2027); set as the current fiscal year-end for a pending regulatory decision because the item gives no date beyond the authority's Thursday announcement.

description: Will DRAM/HBM contract prices remain elevated through calendar 2027, extending the shortage that has raised GPU makers' memory input costs?
outcome: Direction and level of DRAM/HBM contract prices through calendar 2027, specifically whether they remain above 2026 levels or normalize as Micron's 2027/2028 outlook suggests.
period: Full-year calendar 2027; checked against Q4 2027 DRAM contract price releases (TrendForce/DRAMeXchange) and memory makers' Q4 2027 results, reported roughly January 2028.

description: Will Nvidia's Vera CPU platform — the AI-workload server processor management introduced to push beyond GPUs — reach first customer shipments and begin generating revenue by Nvidia's fiscal year ending late January 2027?
outcome: First customer shipments / initial revenue from Nvidia's Vera CPU platform, confirmed by the company.
period: Nvidia's fiscal year ending late January 2027 (annual report ~February 2027); the item gives no shipment date for Vera CPU, so the check date is set at the current fiscal year-end because the item reports the processors are already being offered to cloud customers.

description: How large will US federal AI spending obligations be in calendar 2026, and how much in potential contract awards, as a demand pool for Nvidia's AI accelerators?
outcome: Total US federal AI spending obligations in calendar 2026, against the $7.2 billion reported as reached and the $91.8 billion in potential contract awards.
period: Calendar 2026; set as the year the item reports for federal AI spending obligations, checked against year-end 2026 federal procurement data (USAspending.gov/SAM.gov).
